name: Rosuvastatin
route_note: oral tablet once daily, any time of day
owner: generic (many); Crestor brand held by AstraZeneca

discovery.note: Licensed to AstraZeneca in 1998 for worldwide development.

tagline: High-potency hydrophilic statin with minimal CYP metabolism
summary: Rosuvastatin is a synthetic, hydrophilic, high-potency statin that lowers LDL cholesterol by up to around 50–60% at the highest dose. The JUPITER trial showed it reduced cardiovascular events in people with normal LDL but elevated C-reactive protein.
mechanism: Rosuvastatin competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase. Its hydrophilicity and uptake by the OATP1B1 transporter concentrate it in the liver.

Falling intracellular cholesterol activates SREBP-2, which increases expression of LDL receptors on hepatocytes. More receptors clear more LDL particles from the blood, lowering LDL cholesterol; statins also modestly lower triglycerides and raise HDL.
uses: Primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular events
Primary hypercholesterolaemia, mixed dyslipidaemia and hypertriglyceridaemia

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Rosuvastatin is first approved in the Netherlands.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Crestor.

history.title: JUPITER
history.detail: Rosuvastatin reduces major cardiovascular events in people with LDL below 130 mg/dL and high hsCRP.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic rosuvastatin becomes available in the US.

facts: Exposure is roughly twice as high in people of Asian ancestry, so lower starting doses are recommended.
Few CYP3A4 interactions make it useful in patients on many interacting drugs.

references.title: Ridker PM et al. Rosuvastatin to prevent vascular events in men and women with elevated C-reactive protein (JUPITER). N Engl J Med 2008
